subject: Tenant fabric egress analysis & operator playbook
messages:

Cc: Alice Mooney <alice.mooney@cascadebank.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial questions on tenant egress & proof artifacts

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. CascadeBank's InfoSec team is drafting our final procurement packet and we have a few targeted follow-ups related to tenant fabric egress and operator blast radius. Can you provide:

- A high-level network diagram showing tenant-to-internet egress paths, control plane vs data plane demarcation, and any sidecar/proxy hop points.
- A short narrative (1-2 pages) summarizing how Redwood prevents tenant-to-tenant data exfiltration if a tenant VM/container is compromised.
- Evidence of log provenance for egress flows (where flows are logged, retention windows, and how logs are tied back to tenant IDs).

We are aiming to close vendor selection by 3/20. If you can share these items and suggest a short call with your infra lead this week, that would be great.

Regards,
Jon Harper
Director, Security Architecture
CascadeBank

P.S. we may also need a one-page list of artifacts auditors can request for SOC2 readiness review.

Jon —

Thanks — sending a first-pass packet and proposing a 30-minute walkthrough. Attachments: redwood-network-diagram.vsdx (annotated), egress-matrix.csv (per-customer egress patterns), soc2-evidence-index.pdf (list of auditor-facing artifacts).

Quick summary up front:
- Tenant egress is routed through isolated egress gateways per availability zone; control plane tunnels are separate and only carry orchestration telemetry with mutual TLS and mTLS client certs per cluster.
- Each request is tagged with a tenant_id in the dataplane and in telemetry; KV cache and model inference caches are namespace-isolated.
- We maintain cryptographic attestation for operator actions (API calls tied to operator identity + HSM-backed key ops) and immutable flow logs forwarded to customer-owned logging buckets when requested.

Proposed times for a call tomorrow: 9:30am PT or 2:00pm PT. Ben and Marcus can cover operational routing and egress proofpoints, respectively.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-network-diagram.vsdx (diagram, 1 slide), egress-matrix.csv (spreadsheet), soc2-evidence-index.pdf (index of artifacts)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Jon Harper <jon.harper@cascadebank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial questions on tenant egress & proof artifacts

Jon / Tessa / Marcus —

Following up with the operational detail Jon asked for. High level notes (summary of 6 short bullets, technical ops):

1) Egress topology
   - Per-AZ egress gateways (EGW) run in a dedicated tenant-egress VPC; EGWs terminate TLS to external endpoints on behalf of tenant workloads.
   - EGWs are multitenant from a control perspective but enforce per-tenant policies via strict iptables namespaces + eBPF-based cgroup tagging.

2) Data/control plane separation
   - Control plane (orchestration, model management) runs in a separate VPC with no outbound direct egress to tenant destinations. Control plane only accesses customer metadata endpoints over an allowlist.

3) KV cache & inference artifacts
   - KV cache entries are namespaced and scoped by tenant_id. Cache eviction and persistence events are logged with tenant context. No tenant-shared keys exist.

4) Egress logging & provenance
   - Flow logs collected at EGW and at the host overlay (iptable/eBPF summary). Logs include tenant_id, pod/container id, flow start/end, dst ip/port, and rule-match id.
   - Retention: default 90 days in Redwood-managed hot store; up to customer-configurable archival to customer buckets (S3/GCS) for long-term retention.

5) Failover & SLA behavior
   - EGWs are configured in active-passive clusters inside each AZ. In a full-AZ failure we failover to adjacent AZ with route-metrics preserved; we provide RPO for in-flight inference requests (best-effort) and SLA credits for sustained capacity loss per contract.

6) Threat-lattice mitigations (short)
   - We run periodic red-team exercises on EGW and sidecar code paths; attack lattice doc (kv-cache-attack-lattice.pdf) summarizes hypothesized chains and mitigations (rate-limiting, strong tenant identifiers, circuit-breakers).

I attached the kv-cache-attack-lattice.pdf and a CSV mapping of egress flows by service and customer (egress-matrix.csv). Happy to walk through the diagram live.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv-cache-attack-lattice.pdf (4 pages), egress-matrix.csv (spreadsheet)

Thanks for the packet. A few clarifying asks from our auditor team:

- Can you confirm how operator API calls are attested and how those attestations map back to egress rule changes (audit trail)? We need the chain of custody for rule changes.
- For the failover scenario, what telemetry is captured for requests that were active during the AZ failover (we need proof for potential data loss windows)?
- Are there customer-configurable policies to force egress through a customer-managed proxy (we may need to route through a bank-owned proxy for some outbound destinations)?

If possible, can you share the SOC2 artifact index (the file you mentioned) and point us to the specific doc IDs auditors should request? We will schedule the quick walkthrough after we review those answers.

Cheers,
Alice Mooney
Senior IT Audit Manager
CascadeBank

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Mooney <alice.mooney@cascadebank.com>, Jon Harper <jon.harper@cascadebank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial questions on tenant egress & proof artifacts

Alice / Jon —

Short answers inline and next steps below. Full artifacts are attached or available in the shared drive link.

- Operator attestation & rule-change chain: operator API calls are logged with operator_id, request payload, and a signed event digest stored in our evidence ledger (HSM-backed signing). Rule-change events include before/after rule snapshots and a change-request ticket id. Auditors should request doc IDs: S2-EVID-010 (operator-attestation-process) and S2-EVID-011 (rule-change-snapshots).

- Failover telemetry for active requests: we capture in-flight request traces at the EGW (trace id + tenant id) and at host-level summaries. Forensic traces for the time windows around an AZ failover are exported to the same logging pipeline and can be matched by trace id. See doc ID S2-EVID-022 (egw-failover-traceplay).

- Customer-managed proxy: yes — we support an allowlist and custom egress proxy configuration. Customers can supply egress proxy endpoints and optionally require mutual TLS to your proxy. This is documented in S2-EVID-017 (customer-proxy-integration). For bank-owned proxies, we recommend using our per-tenant route policies which bind destination ranges to the provided proxy endpoints.

Next steps / deliverables by EOD Monday:
- Share Drive folder with artifacts (Drive link above).
- Schedule 30-min walkthrough: I booked 3/17 9:30am PT — invite attached (operator-playbook-ics.ics).
- Ben will follow up on the operator attestation snippets we can redact for auditors. Marcus will provide an annotated slice of the network diagram showing the failover path.

If you need an exported packet tailored to auditors (flattened PDFs + signatures) let me know and we will produce it under the DB-9876 procurement folder.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
